blocks.text: Not all the genes of an organism are expressed at once: different genes are expressed at different times. All the cells of a body contain the same genome, but not all genes are switched on in every cell; specific genes are on in each cell type. Switching genes on and off, and the timing of their expression, is controlled by regulator proteins, and the process is called regulation of gene expression.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Liver cells express the genes for the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase, which breaks alcohol down into non-toxic molecules. Brain neurons have the same genes but keep them switched off.

blocks.prompt: Every body cell has the same genes. Why are liver cells different from neurons?
blocks.explanation: Different sets of genes are switched on in each cell type, for example alcohol dehydrogenase genes are on in liver cells and off in neurons.

items: Same genome in all cells; different genes on in different cells and at different times.
Regulator proteins switch genes on and off.
